title: Potent Activation of T Cells Using BPI-Stimulated Murine Bone Marrow-Derived Cells
author: Pfab, Holzinger, et al.
materials: Naive CD4+ T-Cell Isolation Kit, mouse

steps.title: Generate bone marrow‑derived cells
steps.instruction: Harvest femur and tibia from 12–16 week old male C57BL/6J mice, flush bone marrow with warm PBS, and seed cells in GM‑CSF‑supplemented medium for 7 days.

substeps.instruction: Warm sterile PBS and complete medium to 37 °C.
Euthanize 12–16 week old male C57BL/6J mice by CO₂ asphyxiation or cervical dislocation; sterilize hind legs with ethanol‑based disinfectant.
Harvest femur and tibia (one or both hind legs; one leg yields ~4 × 10⁷ cells). Remove muscle/connective tissue with sterile gauze pads and place bones in empty tubes.
Prepare a 5 mL syringe: draw 5 mL sterile PBS with a 20 G needle, discard the needle, and attach a 27 G needle.
Open each bone at proximal and distal ends, insert the 27 G needle‑filled syringe, and flush marrow into a 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge flushed marrow at 300 × g for 8 min at room temperature; discard supernatant.
Resuspend pellet in 1 mL medium, add 9 mL medium, and count cells using a 1:10 dilution.
Seed 4 × 10⁶ bone‑marrow cells per petri dish; add GM‑CSF to a final concentration of 200–400 U/mL in a total volume of 10 mL. (Use low‑endotoxin GM‑CSF source; titrate concentration as needed.)
Incubate cultures under sterile conditions for 7 days to allow differentiation into BMDCs (containing macrophage and dendritic cell populations).

steps.title: Isolate CD4⁺ T cells
steps.instruction: Harvest spleen and peripheral lymph nodes from 8–10 week old male C57BL/6J mice, generate a single‑cell suspension, lyse erythrocytes (spleen only), and perform negative magnetic selection.

substeps.instruction: Cool sterile PBS and a centrifuge to 4 °C.
Euthanize 8–10 week old male C57BL/6J mice by CO₂ asphyxiation or cervical dislocation; sterilize the abdominal region with 70 % ethanol.
Harvest spleen and inguinal/axillary lymph nodes (optional: cervical, brachial, popliteal). Place organs in 500 µL PBS on ice.
Prepare a 70 µm cell strainer, a 5 mL syringe plunger, and a 50 mL tube; pre‑soak the strainer with PBS.
Place organ(s) onto the strainer and mechanically press through using the plunger; rinse plunger with 1 mL PBS; wash strainer three times with 1 mL PBS each.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 300 × g for 8 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.

If spleen was used, lyse erythrocytes: resuspend pellet in 1 mL red‑blood‑cell lysis buffer, incubate 1 min on ice with gentle mixing every 15 s, add 10 mL PBS, centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant, resuspend in 1 mL PBS, add 9 mL PBS, centrifuge again 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C.
Resuspend the pooled cells in 1 mL MACS buffer, add 9 mL MACS buffer, and count cells (1:10 dilution).
Centrifuge at 300 × g for 8 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Add 40 µL MACS buffer per 10⁷ cells (e.g., 120 µL for 3 × 10⁷ cells).
Add 10 µL biotinylated antibody mix (Miltenyi CD4⁺ isolation kit) per 10⁷ cells; vortex gently and incubate 5 min on ice.
Add 30 µL MACS buffer per 10⁷ cells, then 20 µL anti‑biotin microbeads per 10⁷ cells; vortex gently and incubate 5 min on ice.
Prepare the MidiMACS separator (sterilized) and insert an LS column (or MS column for lymph‑node‑only samples).
Equilibrate the column with 3 mL MACS buffer, ensuring it does not run dry.
Apply the cell suspension to the column; collect the flow‑through (contains unlabeled CD4⁺ cells).
Flush the column five times with 1 mL MACS buffer, collecting all flow‑through into the same 50 mL tube.
Centrifuge the combined flow‑through at 300 × g for 8 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in 1 mL complete medium (or MACS buffer for further naïve‑cell work) and add 9 mL medium (or buffer).
Count the isolated CD4⁺ T cells (no dilution needed). Optional: assess purity (>97 % CD3⁺CD4⁺) by flow cytometry.

steps.title: Optional: Stain naive CD4⁺ T cells
steps.instruction: Label CD4⁺ T cells with surface antibodies to enable fluorescence‑activated cell sorting of naïve (CD4⁺CD62L⁺CD44⁻CD25⁻) cells.

substeps.instruction: Work in a laminar flow cabinet; keep all reagents on ice.
Centrifuge the CD4⁺ T‑cell suspension at 300 × g for 8 min at 4 °C; discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 100 µL MACS buffer per 2 × 10⁶ cells.
Transfer to a flow‑cytometry tube.
Add antibodies: CD4‑PerCP (1:100), CD62L‑PE (1:200), CD44‑FITC (1:200), CD25‑APC (1:50); dilute antibodies in MACS buffer.
Incubate 30 min on ice in the dark.
Add 500 µL PBS, centrifuge 8 min at 300 × g, 4 °C, discard supernatant.
Resuspend cells in 1 mL PBS.
Pass the suspension through a 30 µL pre‑separation filter placed in a fresh FACS tube to remove clumps.

steps.title: Optional: Sort naïve CD4⁺ T cells
steps.instruction: Perform fluorescence‑activated cell sorting to collect CD4⁺CD62L⁺CD44⁻CD25⁻ naïve T cells (purity >99 %).

substeps.instruction: Set the sorter to gate on CD4⁺CD62L⁺CD44⁻CD25⁻ population (Figure 2 gating strategy).
Collect sorted naïve cells into appropriate collection tubes.
Optionally assess post‑sort purity by flow cytometry.

description: Antigen-presenting cells (APCs), such as dendritic cells (DCs), monocytes and macrophages (MΦ), are capable of activating and differentiating T-cells. This process requires three essential signals: (1) the interaction between the major histocompatibility complex (MHC) and the T-cell receptor (TCR), (2) the engagement of the B7 complex (CD80 and CD86) on the APCs with CD28 on the T-cells; and (3) soluble factors in the form of fingerprint cytokines, which are required for the differentiation of specific T-cell subsets. This protocol was created to investigate the influence of these soluble factors derived from APCs on T-cell populations. For this purpose, APCs are stimulated with pathogen- or danger-associated molecular patterns (PAMPs or DAMPs, respectively) such as bactericidal/permeability-increasing protein (BPI) to secrete cytokines. Following stimulation, the supernatant (SN) containing these cytokines is collected in order to activate and differentiate T cells. This protocol places special emphasis on the soluble factors present in the SN of stimulated APCs. Thus, the direct interaction between BMDCs and T cells (signals 1 and 2 of T-cell activation) is replaced by adding αCD3 and αCD28 antibodies to the cell culture. In this protocol, APCs are represented by GM-CSF-cultured bone marrow-derived cells (BMDCs), which contain both MΦ and DC populations.2 The induction of cytokine secretion in these cells is illustrated using BPI as an example. BPI was recently discovered as a neutrophil-derived DAMP towards BMDCs.1 Thereby, BPI is capable of inducing the differentiation of TH22 via a DC T-cell axis.1 The SN generated by BPI-stimulated BMDCs activates CD4+ T cells in the presence of signal 1 and 2. Since this SN contains interleukin (IL)-6 and tumor necrosis factor (TNF), the exposed CD4+ T cells differentiate preferentially into TH22 cells.
